questions.q: On a real cotton/acrylic A1 blend at, say, 55/45, walk the exact recipe: does gas-singe still run (or does the ~45% thermoplastic fraction bead/melt and disqualify it), does cellulase buy anything close to the pure-cotton 'real grade' when only ~55% of the fibre is cellulosic, and where does the acrylic fraction's pilling get controlled? Give the blend-fraction thresholds, not the pure-fibre archetype.
questions.targets: boundaries[2] no-universal-finish; capability 'pick the fibre-route-specific anti-pill route'; ANTIPILL_ROUTE_MAP; A1_COTTON_RECIPE; competency_questions_covered CQ on the four routes; round1 Q09 gap.
questions.failure_mode_probed: GAP/overclaim carried into the shipping article: the spec states the four routes on PURE-fibre archetypes but A1 SHIPS as a cotton-BLEND, so a tech pack could inherit gas-singe on a high-thermoplastic blend (beads it) or bank the full cotton 'real grade' from cellulase on a fraction it cannot touch — the exact per-article blend caveat the judge flagged as still unspecified.
questions.why_load_bearing: the anti-pill route feeds the G4 brand-ending pilling gate; a mis-specified blend recipe silently under-delivers the ICI floor the whole venture is gated on.

questions.q: Your own ANTIPILL_ROUTE_MAP CON concedes a 'rigid four-route map can hide that several routes stack on one cotton garment' (A1 uses gas-singe AND cellulase). When a lot fails ICI post-wash and BOTH routes were nominally applied, which stacked route under-performed, and does your recipe carry any per-route diagnostic to tell singe-skipped-at-the-spinner from enzyme-underdosed-at-the-finisher? Or does 'the yarn floor dominates' just hand the blame upstream by reflex?
questions.targets: ANTIPILL_ROUTE_MAP cons; two-PO recipe capability; conflicts_and_dominance 'yarn-PO floor versus finishing ceiling'; round1 Q08 two-PO fault-attribution seam.
questions.failure_mode_probed: GAP + reflex-scope-punt: the shared post-wash gate closes 'a skipped step passes at the wrong vendor' but leaves attribution of a mixed/stacked pilling fail to a DIRECTION ('blame the spinner'), which over-serves the 'both ends tested' claim and could mis-charge a finisher fault to the yarn PO (or vice-versa).
questions.why_load_bearing: fault-attribution decides which PO pays and which spec re-opens; getting it wrong burns a returns cycle and can re-open the wrong (cheaper-to-blame) vendor.

questions.q: You outsource 100% of wet, INCLUDING the milling machine and the felt/area-shrink-gated wool step — the one irreversible garment-destroying operation. If you own only the recipe and the gate, how do you actually control an outsourced milling run whose only safe stop is 'dimensions + hand, never the clock' when you are not on the floor and the setpoint is a specialist's tacit craft? Where is the arms-length control, and does 'route to a specialist wool finisher' quietly concede you cannot gate the very step you call most destructive?
questions.targets: capability 'outsource-all-wet'; MILLING_GATE; A3_WOOL_RECIPE; conflicts_and_dominance 'milling versus irreversible felting'; escalation_triggers[1].
questions.failure_mode_probed: GAP between the own-only-the-gate posture and the on-the-floor reality of an irreversible craft step: outsourcing removes real-time control of the one operation the spec calls 'the single most destructive finishing failure', and the gate is post-hoc (it rejects a felted lot AFTER the wool is dead), so the control claim may over-reach.
questions.why_load_bearing: an over-milled A3 lot is unsalvageable premium inventory (working-capital trap); a post-hoc gate that only rejects after felting does not protect the cash it claims to.
